page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.32-256 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine powered by AMD EPYC 9J14 processors running at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 32 dedicated physical cores supporting simultaneous multithreading, providing 64 vCPUs. Compute resources are coupled with 256 GB of system RAM, yielding a uniform 4 GB per vCPU memory density consistent with standard general-purpose cloud profiles.

The platform does not provision local NVMe or solid-state disks, requiring all persistent storage and operational file systems to utilize remote network block volumes. Graphic processing accelerators are not present, as the server incorporates zero GPUs. In terms of external network exposure, the instance comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address. Resource density is optimized across compute and RAM without incurring hardware costs for dedicated storage or accelerator components.

VM.Standard.E5.Flex.32-256 fits parallelized workloads that benefit from dedicated core scheduling and predictable x86 instruction execution. It is suited for mid-sized relational database hosting on external storage, containerized application clusters, continuous integration workers, enterprise web serving layers, and batch data processing pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.32-256 is a general-purpose compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 64 vCPUs derived from 32 dedicated physical cores using AMD EPYC 9J14 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The configuration is equipped with 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. This virtual instance does not include integrated hardware GPU accelerators or local NVMe storage, meaning persistent storage requirements must be handled via network-attached volumes. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated core scheduling and substantial parallel compute capability, the instance delivers predictable multi-threaded CPU execution. The balanced resource allocation makes it technically appropriate for mid-to-large-scale enterprise applications, microservice hosting, data processing pipelines, web serving, and distributed continuous integration environments.
